text:
Priya: Quick sync request about scheduler refactor experiments. We're seeing a curious pattern when combining long prefetch windows with weighted tenant credits: sudden p99 regressions for mid-size requests. Can we brainstorm why?

Jorge: Which reg? Any flamegraphs or spans?

Priya: Example host host-73, mix of chat+completion. After switching to weighted-credit allocator (weights favor high-throughput tenants) p50 steady, p95 ok, p99 jumps ~2.7x for 64-256 token requests. Trace shows they keep getting delayed behind sticky long-running aggregates.

Kim: Sounds like credit accumulation + aging issue. Our current allocator accrues credits and then drains big batches, but small/medium requests can age out and miss the current window. Two approaches: 1) credit aging (decay credits over time so backlog doesn't starve), 2) dual-queue: a horizon queue for immediate small slices + main aggregator for bulk.

Priya: I like dual-queue but we need to reason about KV-cache warms. Small horizon dispatches risk cold-kv misses and higher per-token cost.

Jorge: Agreed. What about a hybrid: horizon queue that groups small requests only if they share cache region or recent model key footprint. If we can't find affinity, we delay a short amount (e.g., 8ms) to try to piggyback. That reduces cold-kv overhead.

Kim: Sketch config:                                                                                          
```
dual_queue:
  horizon_max_tokens: 128
  horizon_delay_ms: 8   # try to coalesce similar keys
  credit_decay_half_life_ms: 5000
  main_window_ms: 200
```
If horizon_delay expires we dispatch horizon immediately. Fallback to main aggregator if horizon is saturated.

Priya: Credit decay seems promising to avoid long-tail credit hoarding. But we must be careful with oscillation: if decay is too aggressive we lose throughput for heavy tenants. Maybe decay is adaptive: faster during detected starvation.

Jorge: Telemetry we need: credit_balance_by_tenant, credit_decay_events, horizon_coalesce_rate, horizon_kv_miss_rate, horizon_fallback_rate, and main_agg_starvation_seconds. Also circuit-breaker metric that freezes horizon when main aggregator drop-rate > threshold.

ops-bot: Artifact uploaded: gs://perf-artifacts/dual-queue/1748622000/summary.json

Kim: From quick simulator run: horizon reduces p99 for 64-256 token class by ~3x on mixed workload, but increases kv_miss_rate by ~6%. Net cost delta roughly +1.8% infra. Need canary to validate user-observed latency improvements justify cost.

Priya: Proposal: 1) implement horizon queue prototype behind a feature flag, 2) add adaptive credit decay (start conservative), 3) add telemetry dashboards + alarms, 4) run 2-week canary on a dedicated pool.

Jorge: Also add an opt-in request header x-rw-urgency to allow customers to pin into horizon queue. Make it opt-in so default behavior unchanged. Document in SDKs if we expose it.

Kim: Edge case: long streaming calls that start small then extend. Horizon must attach session affinity to avoid switching execution contexts mid-stream. Otherwise we pay heavy context-switch cost.

Priya: Good catch. We'll require horizon only for single-shot requests or the first chunk with a min_tokens cap. Streaming flows remain in main aggregator unless explicitly marked.

Jorge: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with the config knobs, telemetry and canary checklist. Priya/Kim please add simulator numbers and artifact links to the RFC.

Priya: Adding notes to the RFC now and will include the ops-bot artifact. Thanks all.

Kim: I'll start the staging build with feature flag dq-174862 and post logs.
